definitions.explanation: A public march by a group of people to express opposition to or support for a political or social cause.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}でデモ{行進|こうしん}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A demonstration march was held in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {数千人|すうせんにん}の{市民|しみん}がデモ{行進|こうしん}に{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: Several thousand citizens participated in the demonstration march.

examples.japanese: {環境問題|かんきょうもんだい}に{対|たい}するデモ{行進|こうしん}が{世界各地|せかいかくち}で{同時|どうじ}に{行|おこな}われ、{多|おお}くの{若者|わかもの}が{声|こえ}を{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: Demonstration marches against environmental issues were held simultaneously around the world, and many young people raised their voices.

notes:
A compound of デモ (short for デモンストレーション, demonstration) and {行進|こうしん} (marching). In Japan, demonstrations typically require advance notification to the police and follow designated routes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- デモ{行進|こうしん}を{行|おこな}う: to hold a demonstration march
- デモ{行進|こうしん}に{参加|さんか}する: to participate in a march
- {大規模|だいきぼ}なデモ{行進|こうしん}: large-scale demonstration
- {平和的|へいわてき}なデモ{行進|こうしん}: peaceful march

RELATED WORDS:
- デモ: demonstration (abbreviation, often used alone)
- {抗議|こうぎ}: protest
- {集会|しゅうかい}: rally; gathering
- {行進|こうしん}: march; parade
